speaker: Manmohan Singh
venue: Red Fort, New Delhi (Independence Day address)
quote_english: Because of our Government's efforts for development of agriculture and for protecting the interests of farmers, agriculture has grown at an average rate of 3.3 per cent in the 11th Plan which is substantially higher than the 2.4 per cent we achieved in the 10th Plan.
summary: The Prime Minister stated that agriculture grew at an average of 3.3 per cent in the Eleventh Plan versus 2.4 per cent in the Tenth Plan; official estimates put Eleventh Plan agricultural growth in the 3.3-3.7 per cent range, above the Tenth Plan's 2.4 per cent.

analysis:
The Prime Minister's 2012 Independence Day address compared average agricultural growth in the Eleventh Plan (2007-12) with the Tenth Plan (2002-07), giving 3.3 per cent against 2.4 per cent. In May 2013, at the fourth anniversary of UPA-II, he placed Eleventh Plan agricultural growth at 3.7 per cent against 2.4 per cent in the Tenth Plan.

The lower 3.3 per cent figure was also stated in Parliament by the Minister of State for Planning in 2012. NITI Aayog's later long-run series shows agriculture and allied GVA growing at about 3.56 per cent per year over 2004-05 to 2020-21, faster than 2.74 per cent over 1990-91 to 2004-05.

Both the 3.3 per cent and 3.7 per cent figures are within the range reported by different official sources for the Eleventh Plan, and both exceed the Tenth Plan figure of 2.4 per cent. The claim rests on official growth estimates rather than a contested number.
notes: The Independence Day address was delivered in Hindi; the quote is the government's official English rendering, so quote_is_verbatim is false.
